critic_notes.rationale: This is a mechanical product of two well-documented anomalies (cash-based operating profitability and capex-intensity/investment) with no new economic content beyond "buy profitable low-investment firms," and it is near-duplicative of the batch's own Profit Persistence Investment Deceleration proposal.

The product is internally ambiguous for the stated negative sign because its low end pools unprofitable slow-growing firms (which the profitability anomaly predicts should also underperform), so the short and long legs both contain expected-low-return names, and the underlying "investment anomaly is stronger among profitable firms" idea is already established in the q-theory literature.
Free cash flow scaled by assets is a textbook published profitability/FCF measure, involves no cross-theme interaction at all, and winsorization is a cosmetic addition rather than a hypothesis.

The indicator-times-aqc construction collapses the vast majority of firms (non-acquirers and below-industry-profit firms) to exactly zero, so the sort degenerates into "profitable acquirers versus an undifferentiated zero mass," and the underlying acquirer-underperformance effect is already well published.

Using the second difference of asset growth (deceleration) rather than the level of asset growth is a genuinely distinct construct from the standard investment anomaly and is coherently signed, though ACCEL on annual growth will be noisy and the profitability leg adds little beyond known effects.

Profit per employee is a less-traveled scaling than asset-based profitability and its interaction with the hiring-rate anomaly is a defensible labor-productivity mechanism with matching sign, but coverage will be limited by emp availability and the hiring-rate leg is itself a published anomaly.

The expression contradicts its own hypothesis — dividing profitability improvement by lagged capex intensity means the highest scores go to firms with *minimal* capex, so it mostly reloads the low-investment anomaly, and the near-zero denominator makes the ratio explosive and sign-unstable (negative numerators over tiny denominators) in ways 1% winsorization cannot repair.

Economically coherent and internally consistent conditioning of margin expansion on working-capital discipline, and while the inventory-change anomaly is well known, requiring margin gains to be inventory-free is a defensible earnings-quality refinement rather than a straight rediscovery.

This is essentially an additive stack of two heavily published anomalies (debt/external-financing issuance and profitability change) with SUMRANK providing no genuine conditioning, so the high-scoring tail can be reached by debt growth alone with flat profitability.

DELTA(gdwl/at) is exactly zero for the large majority of firm-years, so the second leg collapses into a massive tie block and the composite degenerates into the ROA-change signal plus a sparse acquirer penalty — and it overlaps conceptually with the archive's already-tested intangible-build/profitability pairing.

This is a direct rediscovery combination of two canonical published anomalies — cash-based operating profitability (Ball et al. 2016) and equity issuance (Pontiff–Woodgate, Daniel–Titman) — added linearly with no interaction mechanism beyond the two standalone effects.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archive's "Capacity Growth Profit Productivity Fade" — (capx − dp)/at is near-mechanically PPE growth and oiadp/ppent substitutes for oibdp/ppent, so only MUL→SUMRANK and the depreciation line item differ.

This is a near-identical clone of the archived "Lean Inventory Margin Expansion" (same SUMRANK structure, same inventory leg, only oibdp/sale swapped for gross margin), and both legs are literally the Abarbanell-Bushee gross-margin and inventory fundamental signals, so it is a cosmetic variant of an already-tested idea rather than a new mechanism.

The second leg subtracts a scaled level (ΔINVT/sale) from a growth rate (sale growth), a dimensional mismatch that makes the "sales growth exceeds inventory investment" interpretation loose, and the underlying inventory-vs-sales divergence conditioned on margin level is close to standard fundamental-signal territory already probed by the archive's inventory signals.

This restates the archived "Capex Roll-Off Cash Resilience" (same multiplicative cash-flow-improvement × capex-decline construction) with only the deflator changed from assets to sales and TREND changed to one-year DELTA — a cosmetic re-parameterization of a signal that already produced a null alpha, with no diagnosis of why the original failed.

Multiplying operating margin by (inverse) fixed-asset intensity is the DuPont decomposition of operating profitability on capital, so this essentially rediscovers the well-known operating-profitability/asset-turnover anomalies in rank form and contributes no genuine cross-theme interaction.

The construction is internally coherent (high signal = all three adverse conditions, consistent with the negative expected sign), but it is a straightforward recombination of two archived conditionals ("Levered Margin Fade" and "Unconverted Capex Profit Fade") that both delivered weak, statistically insignificant alphas, and its legs are individually the known debt-issuance, asset-growth, and profitability-change anomalies.

Replacing the archived level-based profit-per-employee leg with a margin-change leg is a substantive rather than cosmetic change and gives a coherent operating-leverage story, though the employment-growth leg is the well-documented labor-growth anomaly, coverage will remain low, and the proposal does not explain the FMB/alpha sign conflict that plagued its predecessor.

This is a single-ratio change in return on tangible operating assets — essentially the well-documented profitability-change/ROA-improvement anomaly with a mildly rebased denominator — and it contains no cross-theme interaction despite the stated research objective.

The core content (accruals × inventory buildup) is a direct restatement of the archive's "Inventory Accrual Profit Trap" with a sales deflator and a profitability gate, and both legs are themselves canonical published anomalies (Sloan accruals, Thomas–Zhang inventory changes), so it reads as a cosmetic variant rather than a diagnosis-driven redesign.

Economically coherent and sign-consistent, but the third leg (falling interest intensity) is largely mechanically implied by the second (falling debt intensity), so the triple-MIN mostly narrows coverage without adding independent information beyond a known net-debt-issuance-plus-profitability combination.

The expression's "quality gap" (oibdp/at − ni/at) is mechanically just D&A plus interest plus taxes scaled by assets, so the signal primarily sorts on capital/leverage intensity rather than earnings quality, making the stated hypothesis inconsistent with what is computed.

Genuinely novel construction that uses gross-to-net PPE as an asset-vintage conditioner to argue a contrarian, testable reversal of the usual low-investment premium among profitable firms, with hypothesis, expression, and expected sign all internally consistent.

Margin improvement combined with investment restraint has already been tested repeatedly in the archive (Capex Roll-Off Cash Resilience, Lean Inventory Margin Expansion, Hiring Pause Margin Leverage), and swapping in an intangible-growth leg is an incremental variant rather than a new mechanism.

Wrapping IND_ADJ inside IND_RANK is rank-preserving within industry (subtracting an industry-level constant does not reorder members of that industry), so this expression is numerically identical to the archived "Gross Margin Inventory Efficiency" and is a pure cosmetic rediscovery.

This is a sign-flipped mirror of the archived "Aged Asset Underinvestment Trap" with the same three conditioning variables, and its long leg (profitable, old-asset firms with capex far above depreciation) sits directly against the well-documented investment/asset-growth anomaly without any argument for why the aged-asset conditioning should reverse it.

The three-way conditioning on expensed innovation, current margin, and balance-sheet intangible restraint is a coherent and not-yet-tested combination, but COALESCE(xrd,0) creates a large mass of tied zeros so the short leg will effectively be "firms that report no R&D" (an industry/size proxy) rather than a clean opposite of the hypothesis.

The expense-migration mechanism is economically coherent and the SG&A-intensity leg is genuinely new relative to the two archived intangible-build conditionals, though those both failed weakly and this is the third pass at the same underlying theme, so the prior on incremental information is modest.

This is essentially the long-side mirror of the archived "Inventory Accrual Profit Trap" combined with the archived "Lean Inventory Margin Expansion," and its two active legs are the Sloan accrual anomaly and the Thomas-Zhang inventory-change anomaly in barely disguised form.

Conditioning multi-year acquisition intensity on a high-but-rolling-over profitability profile is a substantive cross-theme interaction rather than a restatement of the known acquirer-underperformance effect, with the main caveats being the zero-mass in COALESCE(aqc,0) and the coverage cost of the five-year window.

This is essentially a recombination of two archived signals ("Capacity Growth Profit Productivity Fade" and "Profitable Capacity Instability") with only the denominator of the productivity leg switched from profit-per-PPE to sales-per-PPE, so it is a cosmetic variant of already-tested (and weak) capacity-expansion-plus-fade constructs and largely overlaps the asset-growth anomaly.

The mechanism is thoughtful and the use of after-depreciation margin (oiadp) is a real distinction, but legs one and three are mechanically correlated (a fully depreciated old asset base almost definitionally shows low dp/ppegt), so the "understated depreciation" channel is double-counted with asset vintage rather than independently identified, and the construct sits very close to the archived "Aged Asset Underinvestment Trap."

This is a substantive rather than cosmetic extension of the archive's best-performing R&D discipline signal — moving from current expensed R&D and margin *levels* to five-year cumulative innovation intensity and realized margin *improvement* — with internally consistent legs and a sign direction that matches the expression.

Two of the three legs are lifted directly from archived signals ("Serial Acquisition Profit Roll" and "Intangible Build Cash Conversion Gap"), and the surviving economic content — high accruals (oibdp minus oancf) among acquisitive firms — largely restates the well-documented accruals and acquirer-underperformance anomalies in interacted form.

The signal is close to a triple sort on profitability, sales growth, and falling investment, i.e. a repackaging of the RMW/CMA-spanned profitability and investment anomalies that FF5 already prices, and the sales-growth conditioner adds little beyond the archived "Capex Roll-Off Cash Resilience" idea.

Narrowing the financing leg to short-term debt (dlc) and pairing it with deteriorating operating cash flow among profitable firms is a defensible, internally consistent sharpening of the weak archived "Levered Margin Fade," though it remains adjacent to the known net-debt-issuance and accruals effects and is only a modest conceptual step.

This is largely a leg-swap on the archived "Cumulative RND Harvest No Capitalization" (same R&D-intensity and intangible-restraint gates, with the margin-improvement leg swapped for a cash-margin leg), and the added TS_COUNT(xrd,5) gate is both redundant with the COALESCE-based R&D intensity leg and nearly degenerate (a 0–5 integer that ranks as a mass of ties), while the fourth conjunctive gate plus oancf availability will further thin an already ~0.11 coverage tail.

The three legs are economically distinct and the "innovation converting into pricing power without working-capital absorption" story is coherent, but it is close to a mechanical merge of two already-successful archive signals (cumulative R&D harvest and lean-inventory margin expansion), so the incremental information beyond those is uncertain.

Because MIN-conjunctions are not sign-symmetric, flipping all three legs of "Aged Asset Underinvestment Trap" genuinely tests a different tail rather than rediscovering it, and the post-investment-cycle harvest story is internally consistent; the main caveat is that low ppegt/ppent is contaminated by recent acquisitions and asset write-ups rather than purely "fresh" plant.

Replacing the interest-burden leg of "Cash Deleveraging Profit Harvest" with a non-monotonic maintenance-capex gate is a substantive rather than cosmetic change, but NEG(ABS((capx−dp)/at)) mechanically favors asset-light firms (where both terms are tiny) rather than firms genuinely reinvesting at replacement rate, so a capx/dp ratio centered at one would match the stated construct better.

This is the complementary tail of the archived "Acquisition Integration Cost Creep" with two legs sign-flipped and no new economic content, and it takes the long side in high cumulative acquisition intensity — a well-documented negative predictor (acquirer/asset-growth anomaly) — so the expected positive sign is fighting the dominant known effect with only two soft margin gates.

The construction stacks four conjunctive gates assembled almost entirely from previously tested and weak archive components (sstk issuance gate, intangible-build-with-margin-fade, high-then-fading margin), one of which already came in with the wrong sign, and the four-way MIN on sstk/intan will produce a sparse, unstable long-short tail; the residual signal is also likely just the well-known net-share-issuance anomaly.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archive's "Cumulative RND Harvest No Capitalization" (identical R&D-intensity and margin-delta legs, with the intangible restraint leg merely re-expressed as a 3-year level instead of a one-year change), so it is unlikely to teach anything beyond the already-tested signal.

This is essentially the archive's "Capitalized SGNA Substitution Trap" re-proposed with the expected sign flipped to match its in-sample wrong-signed alpha, which is HARKing rather than an independent mechanism, and swapping the margin level for a margin change does not make it a substantively new construct.

The scale-free (capx−dp)/(capx+dp) reformulation is a genuine and well-diagnosed repair of the earlier at-normalized maintenance term that mechanically favored asset-light firms, though the parent signal's null portfolio evidence and ~8% coverage make a large payoff unlikely.

The expression matches the hypothesis and tests the economically complementary tail of the archive's aged-asset underinvestment result (aged plant with balanced rather than deficient reinvestment), so the positive expected sign is coherent rather than a mere sign flip.

The conditioning set (high margin + headcount growth + deteriorating per-employee productivity) is a near-mirror of the archive's "Productive Hiring Scale Up" and "Acquisition Labor Productivity Break" with only the productivity metric changed from profit-per-employee to sales-per-employee, both of which produced weak evidence.

The acquisition-financing-strain angle (rising short-term debt intensity) is a genuinely new conditioner relative to the archive's SG&A-creep and profitability-trend acquirer signals, the expression matches the stated hypothesis, and the negative sign follows naturally from all three legs.

This is a third-leg swap within an already heavily mined template (MIN of cumulative R&D intensity, margin delta, and one discipline leg — see Cumulative RND Harvest No Capitalization, RND Product Margin Inventory Release, RND Operating Asset Commercialization, RND Payoff Cash Retention), and the substituted leg NEG(ABS((capx-dp)/(capx+dp))) has already been tested twice with essentially zero or sign-flipped alpha, so it is a cosmetic variant rather than a new mechanism.

It reuses the familiar R&D-intensity family template but inverts the economics (externally funded innovation with realized margin deterioration rather than harvest), which is a substantively different tail; the main caveats are that share issuance is a canonical published anomaly likely to drive much of the signal and that high-R&D firms issue equity almost mechanically, so incremental content over plain net issuance is uncertain.

Adding an acquisition-exclusion leg to Fresh Plant Harvest Margin is a defensible measurement fix — gross-to-net PPE is genuinely contaminated by purchase accounting step-ups — but it is an incremental filter on an already-tested signal and the fourth MIN leg risks thinning the extreme portfolio and degrading the existing t-stat of 2.2.

This is essentially the union of two already-evaluated archive signals (Old Plant Profit Cash Mismatch and Aged Plant Catch Up Strain), stacking their legs into a four-way MIN without introducing any new variable or mechanism, so it is a rediscovery whose only likely effect is narrower, less stable portfolio composition.

Substituting the goodwill stock for cumulative aqc flow is a real measurement improvement (persistent, less lumpy, directly tied to impairment risk) rather than a pure restatement of Serial Acquisition Profit Roll, though the economic story overlaps closely with the known goodwill/intangible-intensity anomaly and with the existing acquisition-fatigue family, so the incremental information is modest.

This swaps the deleveraging leg for a cash-build leg in a family that has already returned null results twice (Deleveraging With Maintenance Discipline, alpha -0.003; Deleveraging Replacement Capex Balance, alpha 0.000) while reusing the oancf-plus-Δche pairing from Cash Generator Equity Issue Red Flag, and the underlying story is close to the published cash-holdings/low-investment effects.

This is another slot-swap in the heavily mined "cumulative expensed R&D × improving profitability × restraint" family already tested five times (No Capitalization, Inventory Release, Operating Asset Commercialization, Cash Retention, Profit Stability), and its two non-R&D legs are mechanically linked because falling employment automatically inflates oibdp/emp, so the "productivity payoff" leg is partly a restatement of the hiring-restraint leg rather than independent confirmation.

This is a pure denominator swap on the archived "RND Product Margin Inventory Release" (invt/cogs instead of invt/sale, identical R&D gate and identical gross-margin-improvement leg), a cosmetic variant of an already-strong signal rather than a new mechanism.

Identical to the archived "Fresh Plant Harvest Margin" except the third leg replaces DELTA(oiadp/sale) with DELTA(oancf/sale), a single-leg accrual-to-cash swap that is a standard robustness check rather than a substantively different hypothesis, and it will roughly halve coverage given oancf availability.

This is a mechanical splice of two archived signals — "Goodwill Margin Rollover" (gdwl × high margin × margin fade) and "Acquisition Integration Cost Creep" (acquisition stock × margin × rising SG&A) — with no new economic content beyond substituting the goodwill stock for the aqc flow and the SG&A leg for the margin-level leg.

It is closely adjacent to "Aged Plant Working Capital Squeeze" but, because MIN isolates a joint upper tail rather than a symmetric spread, flipping the inventory leg genuinely targets a different corner (aged-asset harvesters releasing working capital) that the prior test's short leg did not cleanly identify; the hypothesis, expression, and positive sign are internally consistent, though the incremental information over the archived version is modest.

The construction is internally coherent and the rising-interest-burden leg is a distinct financing-cost channel not yet paired with capex expansion in the archive, though it sits in the same crowded "high margin × investment × strain" family that has repeatedly produced weak alphas, and xint/sale changes are partly mechanical in debt/rate movements.
